judged_text: add_members performs no existing-membership check before `group.add(user)`, replacing the old idempotent full-list `usernames=` update with an unchecked incremental insert on the group_users join table. Re-adding a current member — easy in the new UI where the paginated list hides members not on the visible page and the add box is free-form — silently inserts a duplicate group_users row (this schema has no unique constraint on (group_id, user_id)), so the member appears twice in the list and inflates user_count/meta.total.

adjudication.rationale:
In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the new incremental path does `group.add(user)` for each username with no explicit guard against users who are already in the group (or duplicate usernames in the input):
```rb
usernames.split(",").each do |username|
  if user = User.find_by_username(username)
    group.add(user)
  end
end
```
The prior code path used `group.usernames = ...` (full-list style) which would typically be idempotent. The diff does not show `Group#add` or any DB unique constraint, so the claim that this *definitely* creates duplicate join rows / inflates counts is not fully verifiable from the diff alone, but the lack of an idempotency check is a concrete, diff-grounded risk introduced by this change.
